1. **packages/features/bookings/components/PeopleFilter.tsx, `useEffect` auto-push** — Silently mutating the URL/query filter as a side effect on mount changes behavior for every admin globally, not just scoped to the "team bookings" view this fixes (#18026). Any admin viewing bookings in any org — including non-private orgs — will have `userIds` force-set to themselves, which conflicts with the "only apply when private + admin" intent implied by `hasPermToView`. Fix: gate the auto-filter on the same condition that restricts visibility (e.g. only when `currentOrg?.isPrivate` and `isAdmin`), not merely `isAdmin`, and scope it explicitly to the bookings list use case rather than this shared filter component used elsewhere.

2. **PeopleFilter.tsx, infinite re-render / loop risk** — `pushItemToKey` is included in the `useEffect` deps but its identity/behavior isn't shown to be stable (from `useFilterQuery`), and the effect's own trigger condition (`query.userIds` empty) will re-fire every time `removeItemByKeyAndValue`/`removeAllQueryParams` is used by the admin to clear the filter, immediately re-adding `me.id` and making the filter impossible to actually remove — directly contradicting the PR's claim "Admin users can still modify or remove the filter as needed." Fix: only set the default once (e.g. track with a ref/initialized flag, or apply the default at query-initialization time rather than via a reactive effect), so clearing the filter sticks.

3. **Scope/placement of the admin-default logic** — `PeopleFilter` is a generic, reusable filter dropdown component; embedding admin-bookings-specific defaulting logic here conflates presentation with page-level business logic and will leak this behavior to any other place that renders `PeopleFilter` (if any exists or is added later). Fix: move the default-filter decision up to the bookings list page/container (where the "only admins, only bookings page" policy can be enforced once), and have `PeopleFilter` remain a controlled, dumb component.

4. **No test coverage** — The PR only claims "verified through code review," with no unit/integration test added for the new default-filtering behavior or the "can still remove it" guarantee, despite that exact guarantee being broken (see #2). Fix: add a test that asserts (a) default filter is applied for admins on initial load, (b) removing the filter via `removeItemByKeyAndValue`/`removeAllQueryParams` persists (doesn't get re-added), and (c) non-admins are unaffected.

5. **Behavior change not gated by a feature flag / rollout control** — This changes default visible data for all admins across all orgs as a silent client-side redirect-like effect; for a product with this scale, such a default-UX change affecting what data is shown usually needs a flag or staged rollout, or at minimum product/design sign-off reflected in the PR description beyond a screenshot. Fix: confirm with product whether this needs to be opt-in/flagged, and clarify in the PR whether this applies org-wide or only to the specific private-team-bookings scenario in the linked issue.
